territorial_scope.description: Applies to federal positions in the executive branch and to a program run by the NOAA Administrator for U.S. citizens.

evidence.quote: positions within the executive branch of the Federal Government

summary.short: Section 14 directs the NOAA Administrator to establish a hydrologic research fellowship program for U.S. citizens in graduate programs, with research priorities that include applying AI and machine learning to hydrologic modeling. It also gives federal agencies direct-hire authority for fellowship graduates from fiscal year 2022 onward.
summary.long: Section 14 requires the Administrator to establish a hydrologic research fellowship program for qualified individuals: U.S. citizens enrolled in research-based graduate programs at institutions of higher education in listed fields such as hydrology, computer sciences and engineering. Selection must give preference to historically Black colleges and universities and minority-serving institutions, and fellowships last up to 2 years. Fellows are placed in executive-branch positions. The Assistant Administrator for Weather Services sets award guidelines and, with NOAA line offices, USGS, FEMA and the Army Corps of Engineers, publishes research priorities that may include applying artificial intelligence and machine learning to hydrologic modeling. From fiscal year 2022, any federal agency head may directly appoint graduates who completed a qualifying degree and the fellowship, meeting Office of Personnel Management standards, within 2 years of completing the fellowship. The section contains no enforcement provisions.
